title: Review: describing your week
why: Review of the "My everyday life" unit, with nothing new: you bring together reflexive verbs, the time, days, ser and estar and adjectives to describe your typical week. The shared apartment in Valencia makes you use all of it, before tackling the irregular verbs of the next unit.

{"lessons": ["

Describing your week: the tools

Last lesson of the unit: nothing new, but everything you need to describe your typical week. Let's start with reflexive verbs and time expressions.

levantarse
yome levanto
túte levantas
él, ella, ustedse levanta
nosotros, nosotrasnos levantamos
vosotros, vosotrasos levantáis
ellos, ellas, ustedesse levantan

And the three forms given with yo: me despierto (I wake up), me visto (I get dressed), me acuesto (I go to bed).

Time expressions

SpanishEnglish
a las ocho, a la unaat eight, at one
de nueve a seisfrom nine to six
por la mañana, por la tarde, por la nochein the morning, in the afternoon, in the evening
el luneson Monday (one time)
los luneson Mondays (every Monday)
de lunes a viernesfrom Monday to Friday
el fin de semanathe weekend
todos los días, a vecesevery day, sometimes
temprano, tardeearly, late
De lunes a viernes me levanto a las siete y trabajo de nueve a seis.From Monday to Friday, I get up at seven and I work from nine to six.
Los sábados me despierto tarde y desayuno a las once.On Saturdays, I wake up late and have breakfast at eleven.

To say \"OK\", Spaniards say vale all the time. At the end of a sentence, ¿vale? means \"OK?\", \"all right?\".

", "

Ser, estar and adjectives: the summary

What you're sayingExampleVerb
identity, nationality, jobSoy Marta. Es valenciano. Son enfermeras.SER
personality, descriptionSergio es trabajador. La cocina es pequeña.SER
time, dateSon las nueve. Hoy es el tres de mayo.SER
locationEl piso está en el centro.ESTAR
state, moodEstoy cansada. Estamos muy ocupados.ESTAR

Agreement to watch

  • The adjective agrees with the noun or the person: Las habitaciones son luminosas, Lucía está ocupada.
  • Adjectives in -e or a consonant don't change in the feminine: una casa grande, una pregunta fácil.
  • buen, mal, gran before the noun: un buen compañero, un mal día, una gran ciudad.
  • muy + adjective, never changes; mucho + noun, agrees: muy limpio, mucha gente, muchos platos.

Numbers for the week

For times, dates and prices, remember: es la una / son las dos; el veintiuno de marzo but veintiún años; ¿Cuánto cuesta? for one thing, ¿Cuánto cuestan? for several.

Hoy es lunes, el veintiuno de marzo. Son las ocho y estoy muy cansado.Today is Monday, March 21st. It's eight o'clock and I'm very tired.

The quick test: if you're answering \"where?\" or \"how do you feel?\", it's estar. Otherwise, it's almost always ser.

", "

A week in a shared apartment

Here's Marta's story; she shares an apartment in Valencia. Read it out loud and spot the reflexive verbs, the times, ser and estar.

Me llamo Marta y vivo en Valencia. Comparto piso con Sergio, un compañero muy trabajador.My name is Marta and I live in Valencia. I share an apartment with Sergio, a very hardworking roommate.
El piso está en el centro. Es antiguo, pero es muy luminoso y la cocina es grande.The apartment is downtown. It's old, but it's very bright and the kitchen is big.
De lunes a viernes me levanto a las siete y media. Trabajo por la mañana, en una oficina.From Monday to Friday, I get up at half past seven. I work in the morning, in an office.
Como a las dos y media. Por la tarde estoy libre: a veces corro en el parque.I have lunch at half past two. In the afternoon I'm free: sometimes I run in the park.
Los martes y los jueves Sergio cocina. Cenamos juntos a las nueve y media.On Tuesdays and Thursdays, Sergio cooks. We have dinner together at half past nine.
Los sábados limpiamos el piso. Los domingos son tranquilos: me levanto tarde y leo mucho.On Saturdays, we clean the apartment. Sundays are quiet: I get up late and read a lot.

Your turn: replace each detail with your own. Where do you live? What's your home like? What time do you get up? When are you free?

To talk about your home without a possessive, Spanish uses the article where English says \"my\": El piso es pequeño (my apartment is small), La cocina es luminosa. Possessives will come in an upcoming unit.
